unmapped_concepts.fact:household.mortgage_principal: rulespec-be at b105e2b3 has no input for mortgage capital repayments. The only housing-loan inputs are the interest deductions belgium_social_integration_eligible_annual_mortgage_interest_on_property (RIS art. 25 §4) and brussels_apa_eligible_annual_mortgage_interest (APA art. 15), which this mapping feeds from mortgage_interest. No non-test rule text mentions capital repayment, and the PIT reductions module takes no loan input.
unmapped_concepts.fact:person.educational_attainment: rulespec-be has no input that reads completed education. No non-test rule text mentions an attainment level, certificate or ISCED level. Every education input describes current enrollment or training: flanders_school_allowance_education_level, study_allowance_is_higher_education, and the Child-entity family-benefit training flags, including wallonia_family_benefits_child_in_qualifying_diploma_training. Where this mapping binds these, it feeds them from education_enrollment.
unmapped_concepts.fact:person.enrolled_full_time: rulespec-be has no input that tests full-time enrollment. The full-time wording in non-test rule text concerns work regimes (parental leave, the work bonus, unemployment admission, the Flemish jobbonus). The one exception is a Flemish school-allowance parameter citing 'voltijds secundair onderwijs', and that module selects it by education level alone. The student statuses the tree does take are supplied legal statuses, and the rules that consume them contain no full-time test: belgium_self_employed_is_student (RD 38 art. 12bis) and the Child-entity family-benefit training and 'qualifying' flags.
unmapped_concepts.fact:person.realized_capital_gains: rulespec-be at b105e2b3 encodes no capital-gains rule: no non-test module mentions capital gains, plus-values or meerwaarden. The nearest inputs are legal net-income categories that realized gains do not determine. One is belgium_pit_net_miscellaneous_income (Person, CIR art. 6 in taxable_income.yaml), which the module takes as already determined under category-specific rules. The others are the TaxUnit belgium_pit_spouse_{a,b}_article_90_items_1_to_4_and_12_income slots in the art. 127 joint-assessment allocation.
unmapped_concepts.fact:person.rental_income: rulespec-be at b105e2b3 has no input that net rental income determines. (1) belgium_pit_net_immovable_income (Person, CIR art. 6) is a net-income category that taxable_income.yaml 'expects ... to have already been determined under the category-specific CIR 1992 rules', and no module derives it. (2) belgium_social_integration_annual_property_rent (RIS art. 26) lives on Household, and no transform puts a person amount on a Household input. (3) belgium_pit_article_17_non_copyright_movable_property_rental_use_or_concession_income is income from movable property, which is outside the concept's land-and-buildings scope.
unmapped_concepts.fact:person.sex: rulespec-be at b105e2b3 has no input that reads sex. No surface input name and no non-test rule text mentions sex or gender. The one sex-dependent provision found, Brussels social-housing child-bedroom pairing, is left out of the module: social_housing_rental.yaml lists 'exact child-room pairing from person-level sex/age arrays' among what it leaves to separate surfaces. It enters only as the supplied Household count brussels_social_housing_child_bedrooms_required.
unmapped_concepts.fact:person.take_up_seed: rulespec-be computes legal entitlements and has no take-up or participation input. Its only claim-type inputs are eligibility conditions or elections, not decisions to take up the program the rule computes: belgium_social_integration_social_benefit_rights_asserted (a RIS art. 3-4 condition), brussels_apa_required_other_benefit_rights_claimed (an APA eligibility conjunct), and belgium_pit_article_1458_pension_savings_reduction_claimed (a non-cumulation election against the art. 145/7 reduction that also needs pension-savings payments).
unmapped_concepts.fact:person.weeks_worked: rulespec-be has no input for weeks worked in a year. Its work-history inputs are day or hour counts over windows that run back from a claim. Examples: belgium_unemployment_article_30_countable_work_days_since_prior_admission_in_extended_reference_period (312 work days within a 36-month reference period, admission.yaml), and belgium_health_waiting_stage_assimilated_work_days/_hours (windows of one to 36 months, with the length supplied as the separate input belgium_health_waiting_stage_reference_months, waiting_stage.yaml). These need a claim date, count days rather than weeks, and depend on an assimilated-day classification that the module leaves to separate surfaces. Multiplying weekly hours by weeks (a Product transform) would still give annual hours, not hours inside the claim window.
